paragraphs.en: The natural history museum opened an exhibition about ecology with an unexpectedly ordinary image: a tractor moving across a pasture. A sheep and a lamb stood near a hedge, while a bull waited beside a timber gate. The scene looked peaceful, yet the label asked what supported it. Soil, rainfall, fuel, labor, and markets all helped create the familiar landscape. A visitor who imagined nature as something separate from human life had to reconsider. Even an oak at the edge of a field could reflect centuries of choices about grazing, ownership, and the management of wood.
paragraphs.zh: 自然史博物馆的生态学展览以意外普通的图像开场：拖拉机驶过牧场，绵羊和小羊站在树篱旁，公牛等待在木门边。场景看似平静，说明牌却问它靠什么维持。土壤、雨水、燃料、劳动和市场共同创造熟悉景观。把自然想成人类生活之外事物的游客，不得不重新思考。甚至田边一棵橡树，也可能反映数百年来关于放牧、所有权与林木管理的选择。

paragraphs.en: A second room examined extinction. A dinosaur skeleton stood opposite a photograph of a panda, while a model shark illustrated the long history of marine predators. A smaller display explained that a mammal need not be large to matter in an ecosystem. The extinct creature was not a monster from a story; it had lived under particular conditions that eventually changed. A comparison between an ape and other primates showed why simple rankings of intelligence were misleading. Survival depended on suitable relationships and habitats, not on a competition in which every species pursued the same goal.
paragraphs.zh: 第二展室研究灭绝。恐龙骨架与熊猫照片相对，鲨鱼模型展示海洋捕食者的漫长历史。较小的展品说明，哺乳动物不必体型庞大，仍能在生态系统中发挥重要作用。灭绝生物不是故事里的怪物，而是曾生活在特定、后来改变的条件下。类人猿与其他灵长类的比较说明，简单的智力排名为何会误导。生存依赖合适的关系与栖息地，而不是所有物种追逐同一目标的竞赛。

paragraphs.en: The exhibition then followed changing weather across latitude. In one photograph, fog covered a bleak slope; in another, sunshine reached a cluster of flowers beginning to bloom. A butterfly fed beside a bud, and a hawk watched from a pine. Farther toward the tropic, a jungle received heavy rain while a coastal harbor faced severe storms. Hail and thunder could destroy a crop within minutes, but slower changes were harder to notice. Visitors learned why a single unusual season could not establish a climate trend, although repeated observations could reveal a pattern that deserved serious attention.
paragraphs.zh: 展览随后沿纬度追踪天气变化。一张照片中，雾覆盖荒凉斜坡；另一张中，阳光照在刚开始开花的一簇花朵上。蝴蝶在花蕾旁取食，鹰从松树上观察。更靠近热带，丛林承受大雨，沿海港口面对猛烈风暴。冰雹与雷暴可能在几分钟内毁掉庄稼，但较缓慢的变化更难注意。游客了解到，单个异常季节不能确定气候趋势，但重复观察能够揭示值得重视的模式。

paragraphs.en: A model of a gulf connected environmental processes with human industry. Ore extraction removed vegetation, dust traveled through the air, and smog gave a city an unpleasant odor. A bright flame in a refinery produced energy as well as emissions, while water vapor rose from a nearby cooling system. The display distinguished these substances instead of treating every visible cloud as equally harmful. Ozone, too, had different consequences depending on where it occurred. A breeze could disperse pollution locally without making it disappear. Understanding these distinctions helped visitors ask precise questions rather than respond only to dramatic photographs.
paragraphs.zh: 海湾模型把环境过程与人类工业连接起来。采矿清除植被，尘土在空气中传播，烟雾让城市散发难闻气味。炼油厂明亮火焰产生能源，也产生排放，附近冷却系统则升起水蒸气。展品区分这些物质，而不是把每团可见云雾都当成同样有害。臭氧的作用也取决于所在位置。微风可能把当地污染吹散，却不能让它消失。理解这些差别，有助于提出精确问题，而不是只对震撼照片作反应。

paragraphs.en: The final section considered refuge and responsibility. An eagle needed space to hunt, a donkey needed careful treatment, and a small bug survived in ground that gardeners sometimes called a weed bed. A display of sand beside a photograph of famine warned that environmental catastrophe became worse when people lacked resources and political protection. Above the exit, an image of a galaxy suggested an enormous universe, but the museum returned attention to this planet. Conservation was not a search for perfect innocence. It was the patient work of recognizing consequences, protecting vulnerable life, and changing practices when better evidence became available.
paragraphs.zh: 最后部分讨论庇护与责任。雕需要狩猎空间，驴需要得到妥善对待，小虫则生存于园丁有时称为杂草地的地方。沙土展品旁的饥荒照片提醒，当人们缺少资源与政治保障，环境灾难会更加严重。出口上方的星系图像暗示宇宙巨大，但博物馆把注意力重新带回地球。保护自然不是寻求完美无辜，而是耐心认识后果、保护脆弱生命，并在更好证据出现时改变做法。
